title: Reactivity and Extraction of Metals
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Reactivity Series and Extraction of Metals Worksheets
standard_text: The order of metals and carbon in the reactivity series; the use of carbon in obtaining metals from metal oxides; displacement reactions; Earth as a source of limited resources and the efficacy of recycling.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on the reactivity series and extraction of metals: carbon and hydrogen in the series, displacement, oxidation and reduction, electrolysis, ores and recycling. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Carbon can extract metals below it.
key_sub: Metals above carbon need electrolysis; reduction is the loss of oxygen.
body_html:
How to think about it

A metal's position in the reactivity series decides how it is extracted.

  • Series: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, (C), Zn, Fe, Sn, Pb, (H), Cu, Ag, Au.
  • Above carbon: electrolysis. Below carbon: heat the oxide with carbon (reduction). Gold and silver are found pure.
  • Reduction is loss of oxygen; oxidation is gain of oxygen. Recycling saves ore and energy.
Example

Zinc: extraction method?

Below carbon

Answer: heat the oxide with carbon

Example

Copper oxide + carbon: what is reduced?

It loses oxygen

Answer: copper oxide

Common mistakes

  • Thinking aluminium can be extracted with carbon.
  • Mixing up reduction and oxidation.
  • Thinking recycling saves no energy.

faq.q: How do you know which method to use to extract a metal?
faq.a: Look at the reactivity series. Metals more reactive than carbon are extracted by electrolysis; less reactive ones by heating their oxide with carbon.

faq.q: What is the difference between oxidation and reduction?
faq.a: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen; reduction is the loss of oxygen. In iron oxide + carbon → iron + carbon dioxide, iron oxide is reduced and carbon is oxidised.
Ores are limited, and recycling uses far less energy than extracting new metal. Recycling aluminium saves about 95% of the energy.
